title: Graph Theory
motto: Graphs are the data structure of relationships. If your data has connections, you need graph theory.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Graphs are the data structure of relationships. If your data has connections, you need graph theory.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Social networks, molecules, knowledge bases, citation networks, road maps -- all are graphs. Traditional ML treats data as flat tables. Each row is independent. Each feature is a column. But when the structure of connections matters, tables fail.
Consider a social network. You want to predict what product a user will buy. Their purchase history matters. But their friends' purchase history matters more. The connections carry signal.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Graphs model molecules, social networks, and GNNs. Adjacency lists define who connects to whom.
